answer: Each spring is measured at its source and every farm's share is written in the water book, and no farm may draw more than its share in a dry summer. A thread share claimed without a spring fails the book: at the falcon of the source the water must flow where the book says, and a claimed share dries up another farm's field. Faking the rights means bribing the water warden, forging 40 years of measures and paying 24,700, while the basalt entry in the water book is read at every drought, so a share whose spring was never measured is struck off.
